info.title: Open Opus API
info.description: Open Opus — an open, curated catalogue of classical composers and their works. Free, no authentication. The realm's canonical source for work facts, in two modes. SEARCH: `omnisearch` resolves a free-text query (composer + work, e.g. 'Beethoven Symphony 5') into a stable work id, so a MusicalWork canonicalizes onto the Open Opus spine and dedupes against works the user has already rated. BROWSE: `popularComposers`, `composersByEpoch`, `composerByIds` and `worksByGenre` walk the catalogue by structure rather than by name — which is the only path that works for a listener who cannot yet name what they want, and the reason this realm does not need a rating before it can recommend anything.

get.summary: Free-text search across composers, works and genres.
get.description: Searches the whole catalogue with a single free-text `query` (e.g. 'beethoven symphony 5', 'chopin nocturne op 9'). Returns a `results` array ordered by relevance; each element carries a `composer` object and — for work hits — a `work` object. Composer-only hits set `work` to null, so to resolve a specific work take the FIRST result whose `work.id` is non-null. Use a fairly specific query (composer surname + form + number) for a clean top hit.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: URL-encoded free-text search, e.g. 'beethoven%20symphony%205'. Include the composer surname to disambiguate common forms ('symphony no 5' alone is ambiguous across composers).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based paging offset. Pass 0 for the first (most relevant) page of results.

200.description: Search results. `status.success` is 'true' on a well-formed response even when `results` is empty.

get.description: Open Opus's own shortlist of the composers people actually listen to — around two dozen, each with portrait, epoch and dates. Takes no parameters, so it is the one call that answers 'where do I even start' without the caller knowing a single name.

get.summary: Every catalogued composer of one style period.

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.description: Style period, spelled as Open Opus spells it: 'Medieval', 'Renaissance', 'Baroque', 'Classical', 'Early Romantic', 'Romantic', 'Late Romantic', 'Post-War', '20th Century', '21st Century'. An unrecognised spelling returns no rows rather than an error, so pass one of these exactly.

get.summary: Composers by id — several in one call.
get.description: Resolves one or more Open Opus composer ids to full records (complete name, epoch, dates, portrait). Accepts a comma-separated list, which is what makes a composer join over a page of works ONE request instead of one per row.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: One composer id, or several comma-separated: '145' or '145,80,87'.

200.description: A `composers` array, one element per id that resolved.

get.summary: One composer's works in one genre.
get.description: The catalogue's works for a composer, filtered by genre. Note the response carries the composer ONCE at the top level, not on each work, so a caller that needs '<composer> <title>' must join the two itself. 'Popular' is sparse in a way the catalogue does not advertise — Rameau has 57 works and none marked popular — so a browse path should widen Popular -> Recommended -> all rather than treat an empty answer as 'no works'.

parameters.name: composerId
parameters.description: Open Opus composer id, e.g. '80' for Brahms.

parameters.name: genre
parameters.description: 'Popular' (the catalogue's own shortlist of best-known works, any form), 'Recommended' (a narrower one), 'all' (every work it holds — undocumented by Open Opus but live, and the only rung that works for a composer nobody has shortlisted), or one of 'Orchestral', 'Chamber', 'Keyboard', 'Vocal', 'Stage'. NOTE an empty genre answers `success: "false"` with an `error`, not an empty `works` list.

OmnisearchHit.description: One search hit: always a composer, plus a work when the hit is a work.

work.description: The matched work, or null for a composer-only hit.

id.description: Stable Open Opus work id. Use as Work.workId when persisting.

title.description: Work title, e.g. 'Symphony no. 5 in C minor, op. 67'.

subtitle.description: Nickname or subtitle, often empty, e.g. 'Emperor'.

popular.description: '1' if a well-known / frequently performed work.
